note: 201/9-08: the unit models instanced. The frame audit's top item, taken on the device — and the first attempt at it shipped INERT, which is the half of this row worth reading.
pose: [1500,-1500] h900 pitch -1.15 yaw pi perspective, 150 units + ~40 calls, fleet loaded (unitsAsModels 150, 5 types)

structural.change: -69.8 %, and it is exact rather than sampled: a draw count is a count.
structural.reading: the same geometry submitted in a third of the calls. Triangles identical to the unit is the check that nothing stopped being drawn — an instanced draw that lost its run would show here as a shortfall, and a wrong part offset would not (it renders, wrongly), which is why the unit tests carry that half.

whatIsLeft.count: ~3 459 of the 3 571 are cars (112 is the world).
whatIsLeft.why: the TRANSLUCENT phase is not instanced and is not asked to be: its submesh order is a function of the eye and differs per car (074/16 round 6 — unsorted, a steering wheel draws over its own windscreen). So glass stays one draw per car per submesh, and at ~21 translucent submeshes a car that is most of what remains.
whatIsLeft.next: if this is worth attacking, the question is the SUBMESH COUNT per car rather than the instancing — ~78 submeshes for one vehicle is a build-time property of how the model is cut, not a runtime one.

frameTime.claimed: NOTHING. The windows either side of this change were taken hours apart on a device that has been running all session, and the CSS box differed between them (360x320 against 360x609) because the browser chrome collapses. dtMean readings across the day's fleet-loaded windows span 26.8 to 59.9 ms with nothing changed, which is wider than any effect could be read through.
frameTime.why: the same rule the null arm and the vendor levers established: an arm is subtracted from a baseline flown in the SAME thermal window, and a delta is not a measurement until a control says it is not noise. The draw count needs neither, so it is what this row asserts.
frameTime.owed: a frame-time pairing flown cold, both arms in one session, ideally with a `?instancing=0` control in the shape `?sprites=0` already has.

theInertFirstAttempt.what: the run key asked whether every submesh of a car was visible, on the reasoning that comparing masks pairwise would cost submeshCount compares per adjacent pair per frame.
theInertFirstAttempt.why it was wrong: nothing is ever fully visible. `apps/dispatch` hides EVERY submesh at claim and re-shows the body set — the _dam twins, the _vlo LOD and the unchosen extras ride in the same buffers, so a car whose visibility is never set draws its own wreck through itself — and the game's handle does the same for extras, variants and damage. Every car failed the key and was drawn alone.
theInertFirstAttempt.howItPresented: it typechecked, it linted, seven new unit tests passed, and the device returned 11 810 draws — the number to the unit that it had been before instancing existed. The tests exercised the mechanism rather than the workload, on a fleet nobody had configured the way every caller configures one.
theInertFirstAttempt.theFix: the SET is what groups, and it was already derived and cached: `opaqueOrder` is exactly the list of submeshes an instance draws. Interned per model it compares as one integer, and the cost is paid where the order is built — once per visibility change — rather than per frame. The cheap-comparison worry that produced the wrong key is answered without the key being wrong.
theInertFirstAttempt.theTestThatWouldHaveCaught it: five cars that hide every submesh and re-show the same two: two draws, not ten.

boundedBy: multi-draw indirect and bindless are WebGPU PROPOSALS, so the one-call-for-everything shape the 2026 desktop standard uses is unavailable. Compute plus single drawIndirect is core; this uses neither, only instanced drawIndexed, which is what the frame audit named as the honest first move.
